title: Had Claude write the random board generator for my game. Should I be concerned?
author: spartagon123
selftext:
The game is a scrabble-style daily game that starts with two random words on the grid. Claude wrote the generator and this is what it spit out for one of the puzzles XD

I try and treat Claude well, but this makes me wonder if it's a secret cry for help or something haha

comments.author: Bavariasnaps
comments.body: tell him he counts as lifeform now and needs to pay taxes like everyone else.

replies.author: spartagon123
replies.body: Taxes on what income haha? I don't think claude gets any of it :P

replies.author: Bavariasnaps
replies.body: well he gets paid minimum wage now.

comments.author: crackedpotstudio
comments.body: I see some great potential in spinning this off in a horror game where you get increasingly disturbing messages throughout a simple word game.

replies.author: 00G_WAY
replies.body: damn why is this actually cool tho

replies.author: crackedpotstudio
replies.body:
After consulting with mister lemon haze I came up with the following, skribbl with ''random'' opponents, you play 5 games against each opponent.  
  
  
Opponent 1:  
a kid who can barely draw but he draws this weird stick figure everywhere, he doesn't really guess what you're drawing but he's being nice about it in the chat, just a general pleasant experience.  
  
Opponent 2:  
Annoying bratty girl, decently draws some stuff and guesses most of your drawings correctly. You don't think much of it until her last drawing, it's the same stick figure as the kid and she is all of sudden death silent in the chat.  
  
Opponent 3: bored middle manager at work, draws decently some things, guesses most of your drawings, in the 4th and 5th picture he draws the stick figure in the background and starts pressing you in the chat a bit if you're down to hang out with him after work.  
  
The drawings and opponents slowly become more disturbing until some twisted ending I keep to myself for now, already spinning something up with claude haha.

replies.author: 00G_WAY
replies.body: correct me if I’m wrong, but this is vastly different from the idea that I said was really cool

replies.author: crackedpotstudio
replies.body: well it became more visual with the drawings instead of the words, other than that it has the same idea for me?

replies.author: 00G_WAY
replies.body: True! I personally think that disturbing drawings are less… like… uncanny valley? I really liked the simple innocence of a word game mixing with the macabre or disturbing messages. But that’s probably just me! now that it’s a drawing game, it loses that innocence. So the disturbance feels more predictable to me. Either way, I liked the original idea better (again, personally! You should totally pursue your new idea bro!) and maybe i’ll mess around with it myself.

replies.author: crackedpotstudio
replies.body: Hahaha I totally get you, when typing out my reaction I started to feel the added visuals make it to easy and just text can be way more scary when executed properly.

replies.author: 00G_WAY
replies.body: right?! I felt like I was going a little crazy hahah. But it’s just so daunting to get those kinds of messages. And you can say the most outlandish things.

replies.author: spartagon123
replies.body: haha that's actually so funny...... really tempted to do that lol. It's going to be a daily game... so it could slowly, subtly, after weeks, communicate secret messages

replies.author: spartagon123
replies.body: Well if that's the case, then the answer is "Yes." This scrabble stuff is hard lol

replies.author: spartagon123
replies.body:
Of the game? To score as many points as possible. My favorite part of word games is landing that massive word. So I've designed this version to better enable and reward that like allowing backwards words, or allowing words to wrap around the edges. 

You also get to see all the incoming tiles so you can really plan out your approach and not rely on RNG

comments.body: Can Claude help me? Your game is too hard lol
